 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Cardiff City welcome a managerless West Ham after they dismissed their head coach, Nuno Espírito Santo, on Tuesday morning. 
 After back-to-back home defeats to promotion rivals, West Ham have decided to part ways with Nuno, despite his EFL Championship Manager of the Month award last month.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement West Ham currently sit eighth after 13 games, having been unbeaten in the league for nine matches before their consecutive defeats.
 In the statement regarding Nuno's departure, the club confirmed that Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of the squad ahead of the visit to the Welsh capital.
 While no official announcement has been made yet, it has been widely reported by the likes of Sky Sports and the BBC that Scott Parker has agreed to become West Ham's next manager.
 Parker, out of management since leaving Club Brugge in 2022, is no stranger to the Hammers, having spent four seasons in East London and earning Hammer of the Year three years running.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement He could be in the dugout for Wednesday night's fixture, but it seems unlikely given the timeframe.
 As for the Bluebirds, they sit in eighteenth, only four points above the relegation zone, but have shown an improvement in recent games, especially at home, where they remain unbeaten this season.
 After three games unbeaten, Cardiff fell 3-0 to promotion chasers Wolverhampton Wanderers on Saturday.
 Ahead of the clash, Bluebirds boss Brian Barry-Murphy addressed the media, discussing West Ham and providing an injury update.
 "Any changes that West Ham may or may not make, they still have the same players, who have obvious qualities. We know and respect them, but we don't fear them.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "We'll check on Krystian [Bielik] in training today; he's close. I think he has a chance. Rubin [Colwill] obviously was a big positive for us on Saturday, to come back and feel so good after his appearance from the bench.
 "Isaak Davies has a hamstring injury, so he won't be fit for four weeks. Perry [Ng] didn't train yesterday but seems okay. We're hopeful on him. Alex Robertson and Will Fish both didn't train yesterday, so we'll check on them again."
 As for the Hammers, they could be without Konstantinos Mavropanos for the second game in a row following the knee injury he sustained against Southampton, but he did feature in training this week. Kyle Walker-Peters is set to miss out after suffering an injury on Saturday, with Joël Veltman in line to take his place.
 With the departure of Nuno, certain players like Alphonse Areola, Edson Álvarez and Soungoutou Magassa could all be reintroduced to the squad.
 The match is scheduled to kick off at 7:45pm on Wednesday, November 4, and will be shown live on Sky Sports+ in the UK.
